questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go to a place that offered courses in English but where the native language wasn't English so I would have an opportunity to learn a new language.
Additionally, I wanted to go to a place with a foreign and exciting culture different from Denmark as well as a smaller or town where culture is more well-preserved compared to big cities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was generally happy with my experience though it did prove to be more challenging than anticipated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was slightly difficult due to the fact that some of the online information regarding schedules and classes were still being updated and adjusted. However, people (staff and professors) were very friendly and ready to help, either via email or in person.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Online student help desks were hosted once in a while for all international students, not just Erasmus students though I never attended one. Apart from this, I did not receive any assistance when I arrived. 
Professors and staff in the physics department hadn't been informed that I had arrived during the first day of classes and therefore weren't expecting me in class. Additionally, in one of the courses the professor hadn't been informed that I would attend her class at all though I was still able to follow her class. 
Disappointingly, there were no introductory events in order to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was difficult but not impossible to find housing. There isn't a lot of offers but there also aren't that much competition, and housing tend to be cheaper compared to Denmark. 
I found my housing through Airbnb which worked really well though potentially slightly more expensive than renting a room in a shared flat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find a place in the center of Caserta or in Naples for a better social life and more public transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: An application through an online portal which was very intuitive, not very difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote with my coordinator at the host university and asked her questions regarding specific sections of online application portal. She provided quick, useful and sufficient responses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all of the classes that I wanted that were available that semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask your program coordinator at the host university whether any course you might be interested in has been cancelled or moved to a different semester. This happened to a couple of courses I was interested in where that change hadn't been updated on the course website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
A lot of varied and interesting courses to choose from though a more shallow academic level than at UCPH. 
Classes were often rescheduled or cancelled which was frustrating and made coordination with other classes difficult. Professors were very helpful, friendly, and engaging though also often late (depending on the professor, some were always very late, a few were always very punctual) though all tended to change and reschedule class days and times a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took four MA courses and one BA course that was supposed to be a MA course but got combined with the equivalent BA course as it was an introductory course. 
The level and workload was generally easier than at UCPH though still interesting and rewarding.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More one dimensional and primarily lectures, not as much variety. 
One exception include a lot of potential for personalized and interesting lab work as there are few students in the program in general with a high professors to students ratio. The university boasts a big and varied research facility covering a lot of different fields and experimental setups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Physics of Archaeology and Cultural Heritage
Applied Biophotonics
Ecological Climatology
Astrophysics
Machine Learning and AI (Part 1)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
1. Physics of Archaeology and Cultural Heritage
Such a unique and fascinating course but still with a big emphasis on physics where you learn about phenomena and methodologies that are also used in other fields.

2. Applied Biophotonics
Very interesting and thorough course with a good mix of theory and experimental understanding.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Items were as I expected, generally very cheap though some public transportation slightly more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All academics, no clubs or societies really. For that you need to look outside of the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Academic talks and musical performances were put on but that's about it. Some parties and bar nights for students were arranged but outside of university and on the initiative of volunteering students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Karaoke nights or bar nights every other Friday at two different bars in town, a place to meet fellow students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Naples and the surrounding area (Campania). Hike a long the Amalfi coast and go for a swim, visit the old towns and villages, churches and museums, visit Pompei and climb Vesuvius, watch a football match either at Naples stadium or at a square/bar, visit the islands, plenty of stuff to do in the area; both cultural, outdoor, and city activities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult to get used to the lack of structure and relaxed time management, both on campus but also regarding public transportation, traffic, etc. However, that was part of the fun and truly a culture chock (even though it was an anticipated one).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn a little bit of Italian though on an MA level, most can speak good English.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Lack of structure regarding most aspects of life. 
Relaxed attitude to time, meeting hours, and deadlines.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Super friendly and open people!
Delicious food and rich, cheap cafe and restaurant culture, super affordable and easy to go out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The chaos is frustrating but also part of the fun and the cultural experience.
2. The university is lacking both academically and socially but professors are very engaged and accommodating and social connections can be made through other channels like international group meetups in Naples.
3. The surrounding area is gorgeous and have a lot of opportunity for exploration and adventure. The south of Italy is truly a unique, fun, and exciting. ALSO, EAT AS MANY PIZZAS AS POSSIBLE!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go there for the cultural exchange rather than the academic exchange though the place do offer some unique academic opportunities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a bigger culture shock in Europe (the south of Italy) than when I went to Bozeman, Montana in the US (during my BA).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The chaos and lack of structure as well as non-existing social events for Erasmus students to meet each other.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
